summary: Edeltraud Harzer works in Indology and philosophy. She earned degrees from Charles University and the University of Washington and studied under traditional teachers Sri Narayana Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Washington, Puget Sound, Stanford, Indiana, and Texas at Austin.

Edgar Howard Sturtevant was a linguist who studied at Illinois College, Indiana University (A.B.), and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. under Carl Darling Buck). He held academic posts at Indiana, Maryville College, Missouri, Columbia, and Yale (1923–1943).

Edgar Polomé worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Université libre de Bruxelles, Université catholique de Louvain, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts at the University of Lubumbashi and served as Director at UT Austin (1961–1997).

Edgar Thurston worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and other fields. Educated at Eton and King's College London, he worked at Kent County Lunatic Asylum and Madras Medical College, later serving as Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai, and Superintendent of Ethnography.

Edgard Blochet was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religion. He studied at EPHE and INALCO under James Darmesteter. He taught at EPHE (1895–1901) and served as Assistant and Librarian in the Bibliothèque nationale de France's Manuscript Department (1895–1935).

Edith Frances Claflin was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Radcliffe College (B.A.) and Bryn Mawr College (A.M., Ph.D.). She headed the Greek Department at Choate Rosemary Hall (1916–1933) and lectured in Greek and Latin at Barnard College (1936–1945).
Edith Ludowyk-Gyömrői was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her Ph.D. in 1944 at the University of Ceylon, where she studied under G. P. Malalasekera.

Edith Tóth was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and art historian who studied under Lajos Ligeti, János Harmatta, and László Gaál. From circa 1955 to 1965, she served as Keeper of the Indian collection at the Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts.

Edith Wyschogrod was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. She earned her B.A. from Hunter College and her Ph.D. from Columbia University, later serving as the J. Newton Rayzor Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University (1992–2002).
Edmond Yee is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. He served on the faculty of both Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union from circa 1988 to 2008.
Edmund Charles Cox was a historian who was educated at Marlborough College from 1869 to 1874 and subsequently studied at Trinity College, Cambridge from circa 1874 to 1877.

Edmund Hardy was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Mainz, Heidelberg (Ph.D. under Kuno Fischer), Berlin, and Freiburg. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg, University of Fribourg, and University of Würzburg.

Edmund Henderson Hunt was an archaeologist and Indologist. He was educated at Harrow School and Balliol College, Oxford, and served as Chief Medical Officer for the Nizam's Guaranteed State Railway from circa 1903 to 1931.

Edmund Husserl was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig under Wilhelm Wundt, Berlin, Vienna, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1901), the University of Göttingen (1901–1916), and the University of Freiburg (1916–1928).
Edmund Kleinhans was a linguist who studied at the University of Innsbruck under Friedrich Stolz and at the University of Leipzig under Karl Brugmann from 1892 to 1893.

Edmund Leach worked in religious studies and anthropology. He studied at Clare College, Cambridge, and the LSE under Alfred Radcliffe-Brown and Bronisław Malinowski. He held posts at the LSE, the University of Cambridge, and served as Provost of King's College, Cambridge.

Edmund Martin Küttler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna under Leopold von Schroeder, Berlin, and Graz. He worked at the Institut für Kulturforschung, taught at Masaryk University, and served as Director of the Moravian Museum (1939–1945).

Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Leipzig (Ph.D.), also studying under Hermann Oldenberg. He taught Latin at Vassar College in 1890 and served as Professor of German and French at University School.
Edmund Stengel studied under Nikolaus Delius and Friedrich Christian Diez from circa 1865 to 1868.

Edmund W. Smith was an archaeologist and Indologist. In 1886, he became Assistant Archaeological Surveyor for the North-West Provinces and Oudh with the Archaeological Survey of India, and in 1898, he was appointed Curator of the State Museum, Lucknow.
